title: Ethiopian Meskel Celebration
community: Ethiopian Orthodox Christians — Meskel (Finding of the True Cross, September 27)
author: Mama Tigist

heritage.origin: All of Ethiopia — Meskel is celebrated on September 27 every year
heritage.history: Meskel (Finding of the True Cross) is one of the most important holidays in the Ethiopian Orthodox calendar — celebrated with a bonfire (Demera) decorated with yellow daisies and lit on September 27. After the bonfire ceremony, the feast begins. The Meskel feast is distinctive for its abundance of meat (the end of the Apostles' Fast that precedes it), yellow colour symbolism (the daisies), and the honey wine that flows freely.

desc: Ethiopian Meskel Feast — the celebration after the Apostles' Fast: Doro Wat (ETH061), Key Wat (ETH021), Tibs (ETH022), Gomen (ETH106), Ayib (ETH096), and the first Tej (ETH215) of the season. The yellow-daisy celebration feast marked by abundant meat after the fast.
longDesc: Meskel is the post-fast meat celebration — after the Apostles' Fast when meat was prohibited, the feast breaks with the richest Ethiopian dishes. The bonfire night is followed by a feast that is both spiritual celebration and joyful indulgence.
steps: Day before: make Doro Wat and Key Wat.
Day of: make tibs fresh. Warm wats.
chefTips: Meskel must have both Doro Wat and Key Wat — both are non-negotiable.
Serve with the first tej of the season.
commonMistakes: Making only one wat — Meskel demands abundance.
healthBenefits: High protein feast after a fasting period.
culturalNote: Meskel is the feast after the bonfire — the smell of the Demera burning, the yellow daisies on the fire, and then the gathering to eat Doro Wat and Key Wat together. It is one of Ethiopia's most joyful religious celebrations.
